notes:
Summary: EU-headquartered regtech provider focused on automated compliance workflows for banks. Looking for private VPC deployment (no hosted traffic), strict EU data residency, KMS integration with customer-managed keys (AWS KMS with HSM-backed CMKs), and comprehensive audit logging for model inputs/outputs and admin actions. Currently in architecture validation phase; security & legal running parallel reviews.

Recent activity timeline:
- 2026-02-05: Intro call (AE + SE). High-level requirements captured; Archway sent sample compliance checklist. (ff-20260205-archway-intro-call)
- 2026-02-12: Technical deep-dive with infra + security (SE present). Discussed VPC topology, egress controls, and KMS. Action: Redwood to provide reference VPC diagram and KMS integration notes. (ff-20260212-archway-td)
- 2026-02-20: Security follow-up; Archway requested audit log retention policy and encryption-at-rest details. Legal requested contract language for EU-only processing. (ff-20260220-archway-security-psc)
- 2026-03-02: Network team asked for Transit Gateway architecture versus VPC Peering cost/latency tradeoffs. Provided preliminary notes via Gmail (thread-CAAxZb1_archway_security_review).
- 2026-03-09: Internal Redwood call to align on POC scope and resource needs (SE/AE/CSM).

Architecture fit notes (from SE):
- Preferred topology: Customer VPC peered to Redwood Private enclave via AWS Transit Gateway; Redwood control plane remains in customer-managed account (private control plane) or in a dedicated Redwood-managed account with strict peering and IAM roles.
- Subnets: Dedicated private subnets for inference nodes (no public IPs), separate management subnet allowing admin access from customer admin CIDR via bastion + SSM.
- Inbound: Minimal; only management access from specific admin IP ranges over SSH/SSM. No direct inbound from internet to inference nodes.
- Outbound: Strict egress to customer-managed logging/KMS endpoints and to Redwood managed metrics endpoints over designated NAT/egress endpoints. Customer requires egress filtering (allowlist).
- KMS: Customer-managed CMKs in AWS KMS with key policy granting Redwood service principal Encrypt/Decrypt only within their account. HSM-backed CMKs mandatory for production. Need guidance on envelope encryption for token caches and model artifacts.
- Audit logging: Detailed audit stream required (request metadata, partial prompts meta, model responses hashed for traceability) exported to customer CloudWatch/CloudTrail and routed to central SIEM. Retention policy: min 2 years; support for legal hold.
- Regions: EU-first requirement. Proposed primary regions eu-west-1 (Ireland) and eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) for failover; ask about availability of specific GPU SKUs in both regions.
- Data residency: All model inputs/outputs and logs must remain in EU boundary. No outbound replication to non-EU without explicit consent.

POC scope proposed:
- 4-week POC: 2 dedicated inference nodes in eu-west-1, sample latency SLO tests for chat use-case (95th pct <200ms token latency for short prompts), KMS envelope encryption demo, and audit log export to Archway SIEM.
- Deliverables: Reference VPC diagram, runbook for key rotation, audit log schema, and cost estimate for private vs dedicated.

Quotes / paraphrases from Archway stakeholders:
- "We cannot have any PII leave the EU region — contract clause non-negotiable." — Head of Legal
- "We need KMS control and proof that keys never leave our account." — Infra Lead

Open action items / next steps:
- Redwood: Provide detailed VPC reference diagram (TGW and peering options) + estimated monthly cost delta (due 2026-03-17).
- Archway: Share network contact and CIDR ranges for peering; confirm preferred region SKU availability window.
- Legal: Draft data residency amendment; coordinate with Redwood legal on acceptable language.

Potential objections / blockers: legal/data residency; customer-run KMS policy complexity; need for HSM-backed keys may push ARR up. Procurement cycle estimate 6-10 weeks after POC if POC successful.
